title: Połoniny and Dark Skies: Seven Off-Grid Days in the Bieszczady
subRegion: The Bieszczady & the San Valley, Podkarpackie

bestPeriod.window: late May to late June, then mid-September to mid-October
bestPeriod.avoid: July-August (school holidays fill Wetlina and Ustrzyki Górne); November-March (forest roads unploughed, most agroturystyka closed)

transport.note: €130, €220 (car hire from Rzeszów, shared, plus fuel)

gatewayAirport: Fly Rzeszów-Jasionka (RZE); 150 km / 2 h 45 min via DK84 and DW894. Kraków (KRK) is 300 km / 4 h 30 min. Rail reaches only Zagórz or Ustrzyki Dolne; the last 40-60 km needs a car.
summary: Poland's far south-eastern corner is a landscape emptied by history. You sleep in wooden cabins with a stove you feed yourself, climb onto the połoniny, bare grass ridges running above the beech forest like a spine…
hook: Poland's far south-eastern corner is a landscape emptied by history. You sleep in wooden cabins with a stove you feed yourself, climb onto the połoniny, bare grass ridges running above the beech forest like a spine, and come down into valleys where all that is left of a village is apple trees and a stone-walled cemetery. Bears are real here. So is the darkest sky in Poland. It suits self-sufficient walkers who want silence more than services.

snapshot.Difficulty: Moderate (600-900 m ascent days, no scrambling)
snapshot.Start / End: Wetlina → Wetlina (loop, with two base changes)
snapshot.Getting there: Fly Rzeszów-Jasionka (RZE); 150 km / 2 h 45 min via DK84 and DW894. Kraków (KRK) is 300 km / 4 h 30 min. Rail reaches only Zagórz or Ustrzyki Dolne; the last 40-60 km needs a car.

itinerary.title: Arrival and the first ridge
itinerary.morning: Collect the car at Rzeszów-Jasionka, stock up at a Rzeszów supermarket, Wetlina's shops carry basics only, and take DK84 to Sanok, then DW897 through Baligród and Cisna.
itinerary.afternoon: Pause in Cisna for the Bieszczadzka Kolejka Leśna terminus at Majdan, a 760 mm narrow-gauge forest railway that once hauled timber and now runs tourist trains on two lines: **Majdan-Balnica** (9 km, about two hours there and back) and the short steam-hauled **Majdan-Solinka** (1 h 15). The **Majdan-Przysłup** branch is currently closed. In June and September trains run Tuesday to Sunday at 09:30 and 12:00, daily except Monday in July and August with extra departures; the fare on either line is 47 PLN (~€11) normal, 37 PLN reduced (2026 tariff). Book online at bki.systembiletowy.pl or buy at the Majdan window; the schedule is seasonal and thin.
itinerary.evening: Check into Wetlina, light the stove, and walk the 4 km valley track along the Wetlinka before dark. Dinner at Chata Wędrowca, whose oversized *naleśniki* are the single most famous plate in the range.

itinerary.title: Połonina Wetlińska and Chatka Puchatka
itinerary.morning: Start from Przełęcz Wyżniańska or the Stare Sioło trailhead in Wetlina and climb the red trail through beech into open grass. The forest ends abruptly, that transition is the whole point of a połonina.
itinerary.afternoon: Reach Chatka Puchatka, the small stone shelter at roughly 1,228 m on the Wetlińska ridge. It serves hot tea and *żurek* to walkers and sleeps a handful on mattresses. Traverse east toward Roh for the full ridge line.
itinerary.evening: Descend to Brzegi Górne or retrace your line. Wetlina sits inside the Park Gwiezdnego Nieba «Bieszczady», the dark-sky reserve covering the national park plus the Ciśniańsko-Wetliński and Doliny Sanu landscape parks. Give your eyes twenty minutes.

itinerary.title: Forest railway and the abandoned villages
itinerary.morning: Ride the Kolejka Leśna out of Majdan up the Solinka valley, slow, wood-smoke-scented, and the clearest lesson in how this landscape was logged.
itinerary.afternoon: Drive north to Turzańsk and its 1801 Greek Catholic cerkiew, one of eight Polish entries on the UNESCO Wooden Tserkvas of the Carpathian Region list, then on to Smolnik nad Sanem, whose 1791 tri-partite church stands alone on a knoll with no village left around it.
itinerary.evening: Relocate east to Lutowiska and eat early: village kitchens close around 19:00 out of season. Read up on Akcja Wisła, the 1947 deportation that emptied the Boyko and Lemko settlements you drove through today.

itinerary.title: Tarnica and Szeroki Wierch
itinerary.morning: Drive to Wołosate, the last village before the Ukrainian border, and pay the Bieszczadzki Park Narodowy day entry at the kiosk, 11 PLN (~€2.55) adult and 5.50 PLN reduced under the 2026 visitor regulations, payable at the information-and-ticket points, online or by phone. Cash is safest.
itinerary.afternoon: Climb the red trail to Tarnica, 1,346 m, the highest summit in Poland outside the Tatras, marked by a metal cross. If the weather holds, continue over Szeroki Wierch toward Krzemień and Bukowe Berdo, exposed, and unfriendly in wind.
itinerary.evening: Descend to Ustrzyki Górne. Wild camping is illegal throughout the national park; the sanctioned option is the park's designated bivouac and campsite areas at Ustrzyki Górne, Bereżki and Wetlina, used only with a ticket.

itinerary.title: Połonina Caryńska and the Muczne bison country
itinerary.morning: Take the short sharp climb from Przełęcz Wyżniańska onto Połonina Caryńska, 1,297 m. It is the most photographed ridge in the Bieszczady precisely because it is a two-hour ascent with a five-hour view.
itinerary.afternoon: Drive the Lutowiska-Muczne forest road east into the Tarnawa basin. This is the core bison range; the show enclosure and observation point near Muczne gives a reliable sighting when the wild herd will not cooperate.
itinerary.evening: Continue to Tarnawa Niżna, one of the villages erased after 1947, then back. Cook at the cabin. Signal disappears entirely along this road, so tell someone your plan before you set off.

itinerary.title: Otryt, Krywe and the San gorge
itinerary.morning: Cross to the Otryt ridge above Zatwarnica. The blue trail along the crest gives the long southward view over the whole połonina chain, the one photograph that explains the geography.
itinerary.afternoon: Drop into the San gorge to Krywe, an abandoned Boyko village where a ruined church tower, orchard trees and gravestones sit in a meadow. Drive rather than walk in and your clearance earns itself here.
itinerary.evening: Base at Chmiel or Zatwarnica: these are the darkest nights of the trip, with the Milky Way core low in the south from late May and no meaningful light dome anywhere on the horizon.

itinerary.title: Solina, cerkwie and the drive out
itinerary.morning: Drive west to the Solina reservoir. Walk the crown of the Zapora Solińska, the largest dam in Poland at around 82 m high, then take a passenger boat with **Port Solina**, whose Werlas fleet runs hour-long cruises at 50 PLN (~€12) adult and 40 PLN for children up to 15, and which also works two ferry routes across to Polańczyk, 25 PLN one-way to the Cypel landing, 30 PLN to the Amfiteatr (2026 tariff).
itinerary.afternoon: Spare 90 minutes on the drive north for Chotyniec, near Radymno: an early-17th-century UNESCO cerkiew, the finest of the Polish tserkvas and entirely off the Bieszczady circuit.
itinerary.evening: Return the car at Rzeszów-Jasionka. Late departures from RZE are few, so build in a Rzeszów night if you fly before mid-morning.

accommodationStrategy.name: Chata Wędrowca
accommodationStrategy.description: on DW897 at the Połonina Wetlińska trailhead, so Day 2 starts on foot. Its kitchen runs later than anything else in the valley and it is the informal exchange for trail conditions.
accommodationStrategy.booking: 4-8 weeks ahead for June and September weekends, direct; walk-ins fail in season.

accommodationStrategy.name: Bacówka PTTK pod Małą Rawką
accommodationStrategy.description: a bunk-style PTTK hut below Mała Rawka, midway between Wetlina and Ustrzyki Górne, Caryńska and Wielka Rawka are both a morning away. Wood heat, communal drying, no frills.
accommodationStrategy.booking: direct by phone; beds are not held without confirmation.

accommodationStrategy.name: Zajazd pod Caryńską
accommodationStrategy.location: Ustrzyki Górne (guesthouse) and a Siedlisko Carpathia-style agroturystyka near Lutowiska
accommodationStrategy.description: the Zajazd is the practical base for the Tarnica and Caryńska days, with parking and late food. Pair it with a private agroturystyka cabin for the Otryt nights, wood stove, well water, no neighbours.
accommodationStrategy.booking: agroturystyka direct with the owner by phone or Facebook, not platforms; 6-10 weeks ahead for September.

logistics.connectivity: assume no signal in Wołosate, Tarnawa, Muczne and the upper San; download offline map layers. Cabins rarely have wifi.
logistics.emergency: 112. Mountain rescue is Bieszczadzka Grupa GOPR; install the Ratunek app, which transmits coordinates. Response into the far valleys is slow, carry a kit and a headtorch.
logistics.weather: the połoniny sit 400-500 m above the valleys, open and wind-scoured. Fog closes the ridge without warning and September nights drop below freezing; carry a shell and a warm layer.
logistics.bookingWindows: June and September weekends fill 6-10 weeks out; midweek, a fortnight. The 1-3 May and 15 August long weekends are the worst of the year.
logistics.money: złoty. Cards work in Ustrzyki Dolne, Cisna and larger guesthouses; carry 300-500 PLN cash for park entry, karczmas, the railway and honesty-box parking. No ATM between Cisna and Ustrzyki Dolne.
logistics.transportRules: no vignette in Poland. Fuel in Ustrzyki Dolne or Baligród, nothing reliable on the loop between them. Forest roads behind a barrier or a *zakaz wjazdu* sign are closed to private cars, and the fine is real.
logistics.permits: Bieszczadzki Park Narodowy charges daily entry at staffed trailheads (Wołosate, Ustrzyki Górne, Wetlina, Brzegi Górne). Inside: marked trails only, dogs on lead, no fires, no wild camping, no picking. Trails close after storms, read the park notice board.

proTips: Climb Połonina Wetlińska for sunset, not sunrise. The ridge faces west, day-trippers are gone by 17:00, and Chatka Puchatka will still make you tea before you descend by headtorch.
Buy the park entry ticket as a multi-day pass at the first kiosk if one is offered, it is cheaper than four separate day tickets and saves queuing at Wołosate on a Saturday.
Forage on the Cisna and Baligród side, in state forest, and keep the park days clean. Ask in any village shop where the *prawdziwki* are running: people name the valley, never the spot.
The Kolejka Leśna sells out in July but runs half-empty in late September. Ride it on a weekday and you may be the only foreigner on board.

For the dark sky, drive ten minutes up the DW897 above Wetlina and pull into a forest lay-by rather than standing in the village. New moon plus a clear front behind an autumn cold snap is the combination worth planning around.
Greet everyone you pass with *dzień dobry*, silence reads as rude, and skip Solina in August, when it is a domestic resort. In late September the lake is empty and the boats still run.

raw.Access requirements: DW897 (Cisna-Wetlina-Ustrzyki Górne), DW896 (Ustrzyki Dolne-Lutowiska-Ustrzyki Górne) and the Duża Pętla Bieszczadzka loop are potholed but fine in a hatchback. High clearance matters on three approaches: the forest road from Lutowiska to Muczne and Tarnawa Niżna, the track to Chmiel and along Otryt, and the drogi leśne toward Krywe and Hulskie. These rut deeply after rain; clearance, not 4x4, is the real constraint. Many cabins end with a 200-800 m walk-in.
raw.Isolation level: 4/5: Wetlina and Ustrzyki Górne each hold a shop and a bar; between them, nothing. From a Muczne or Otryt cabin the nearest 24-hour anything is 40 minutes away.
raw.Foraging rules: In Polish state forest (Lasy Państwowe) picking mushrooms and berries for personal use is free and legal, no permit, no quota beyond "personal use", and no raking the litter layer. Inside Bieszczadzki Park Narodowy all picking is banned outright, including blueberries; the boundary is signed but not fenced. Blueberry (*borówka*) and *prawdziwek* (penny bun) are the September staples.
raw.Wildlife protocol: Brown bear, wolf, lynx and European bison all live here; the Bieszczady bison herd, re-established from 1963 releases, is the largest free-roaming group in the Polish Carpathians. Make noise on forest tracks at dawn and dusk, never leave food in a car boot, and store rubbish indoors. Meeting a bear, do not run, back away, talking. Bison are the likelier danger: placid-looking, and they charge inside 50 m, especially cows with calves around Muczne.
raw.Off-grid utilities: A *koza* wood stove, a boiler needing an hour's notice for hot water, well or spring water (drinkable, but ask), a septic tank, mains power or a solar bank. Signal is absent in the Wołosate, Tarnawa and upper San valleys, patchy in Wetlina, and returns on the ridges.
